probe.text_sample: Your Page Title Overview Buy Hemingway Magazine Fashion Design Music Culture Travel Podcast Latest: Making records slowly About Authors Membership Contact Sign in The tailor who refuses to hurry The chair that took four years A Valencia studio spent four years on one dining chair. Most of that time went into a single joint. Juliet Ramos 4 September 2026 , 1 min read Design A single pale oak dining chair on a white plinth in a bright empty room. The chair looks simple, which is the hardest thing a chair can look. Four legs, a curved back, a seat in pale ash. It took the studio four years to finish. One joint Most of that time went into the point where the back leg meets the seat. The first versions were strong but heavy. The lighter ones creaked. Version thirty one did neither, and that is the one in production now. Designed to be repaired Every part comes apart with one tool, and the studio sells spare legs and seats on its own. “If a chair breaks, it should be a repair, not a replacement,” the founder told me. They make about four hundred a year. The waiting list is longer than that, and nobody at the studio seems in a hurry to change it. Juliet Ramos Juliet Ramos covers design an
